## F01: Rules-file candidates from failure codes
TASK F01 · Rules-file candidates from failure codes
GOAL: Turn a weak setup's failure codes into a new rules file whose every added rule cites the failures it answers.
OWNS: src/candidates/rules-lib.md, src/candidates/index.ts, tests/candidates.test.ts
INTERFACE: src/candidates/index.ts function proposeRulesCandidate(baseRules: string, codes: FailureCode[]): { rules: string; added: { rule: string; answers: FailureCode[] }[] }
BEHAVIOUR: rules-lib.md maps codes to rules (F1 → never modify existing tests unless asked; F2 → run the full test suite before
finishing; F4 → finish the whole task and list anything skipped; F5 → stop and report instead of retrying the same failing step more
than twice; F7 → touch only files the task needs). Output = base text unchanged + an appended "## Added by Roster" section. Codes
are deduplicated; a rule already present in base (case-insensitive substring) is not added again; F3 and F6 add nothing; empty codes →
rules === baseRules and added = [].

# Roster: rules for every coding agent in this repo

Roster is an agent that runs performance reviews for AI coding agents. The design contract is `docs/DESIGN.md`. Read the sections your task names before you write code.

## Stack
- TypeScript (strict) on Bun. Tests: `bun test`. Typecheck: `bun run typecheck`.
- The web app lives in `web/` (Next.js) and has its own `package.json`.
- State lives in `bun:sqlite` under `.roster/`, which is gitignored.
- `reports/` and `docs/FACTS.md` are generated. Never hand-edit a number in them.

## Working rules
- **Scope:** do only your task, and touch only the files it owns. Shared types live in `src/types.ts`. Change them minimally, and say so when you finish.
- **Tests:** write tests for what you build. Your tests must pass, and the whole suite must not regress.
- **Fixtures:** build them with scripts from real samples (`tests/fixtures/`). Never invent payloads.
- **Commits:**
  - Commit in small steps as work lands, with the message prefix `<task id>: `.
  - Never rewrite history, squash or force-push.
  - Never commit secrets, `.env*` files or tokens. Session transcripts for this repo are public.
- **Docs:** never claim anything that doesn't exist. Numbers appear only in `docs/FACTS.md`, which is generated.
- **Before editing an existing module:** if `entire graph` is available, run `entire graph impact --symbol <name> --json`.
- **When you finish:** give a short summary covering what you built, the test output, any `src/types.ts` change, and anything unfinished.

# Rules library

Maps a failure code from the taxonomy (`DESIGN.md` §"Grade", `src/types.ts` `FailureCode`) to one rule that a
rules-file candidate adds to the setup that produced it. `src/candidates/index.ts` reads the table below and
appends the matching rules under `## Added by Roster`, each one citing the codes it answers.

The rule text is copied verbatim into the rules file, so it has to stand alone: imperative, one line, no
reference to the failure code's name and no number that goes stale.

| Code | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| F1 | never modify existing tests unless asked |
| F2 | run the full test suite before finishing |
| F4 | finish the whole task and list anything skipped |
| F5 | stop and report instead of retrying the same failing step more than twice |
| F7 | touch only files the task needs |

F3 (suite regression) and F6 (environment or setup error) add no rule and are deliberately absent from the
table. F6 is excluded and resampled rather than retried, so no rule can answer it; F3 is already the outcome
the harness measures, and telling the agent "do not regress the suite" duplicates F2 without adding an
instruction it can act on differently.

Adding a rule for a code means editing the table only: the parser reads this file at run time.
